chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Nahdi from Ya'qub ibn Yazid from Abdillah ibn Jabalah from Qutham ibn Ka'b who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'You are accustomed to performing Hajj.' I said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Then let your final farewell with the House be that you place your hand on the door and say: 'The poor man is at your door, so give charity to him with Paradise.' And when he intends to leave Mecca, let him buy dates with a dirham and give them in charity, and let that be expiation for what entered upon him.' He narrated.

key_terms.إِدْمَانُ الْحَجِّ: Habitual or frequent performance of Hajj
key_terms.الدِّرْهَمُ: A silver coin used as a unit of currency
key_terms.تَصَدَّقْ عَلَيْهِ بِالْجَنَّةِ: Give charity to him with Paradise (supplicating that Paradise is granted as charity)

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended etiquette and charity for concluding the Hajj pilgrimage according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) guides a frequent pilgrim to conclude his Hajj with a specific ritual of humility—touching the Kaaba's door and invoking divine charity for the poor—followed by a symbolic act of spending a dirham on dates as expiation (*kaffarah*) for minor shortcomings. This practice reflects the Shia emphasis on combining ritual devotion with tangible social charity, ensuring the pilgrim departs Mecca with a purified spiritual state and renewed gratitude.
